title: Discrepancy in adding money to the wallet
text:
I have a serious Concern regarding USD/INR exchange rate and transparency of charges

I am disappointed with the way USD deposits are being processed through INDmoney/Federal Bank. I recently tried to deposit ₹50,000 into my US wallet, and the app showed an exchange rate of ₹96.25/USD, while the prevailing USD/INR rate at the time was around ₹94.26/USD.

This represents a difference of approximately ₹1.99 per USD, or 2.1%, which is significant for a currency conversion. For a ₹50,000 transaction, this exchange-rate difference alone can materially reduce the USD amount received.

The app also displayed ₹74.89 GST and ₹8,321 indicative TCS. I understand that TCS is refundable and therefore should not necessarily be considered a permanent cost. However, the exchange-rate spread is a separate issue and needs much greater transparency.

My concern is not simply about paying a fee — it is about fair and transparent valuation of the money being converted. If Federal Bank/INDmoney is applying a currency-conversion markup, customers should clearly be shown the reference USD/INR rate, the markup/spread being applied, and the exact amount being charged because of that spread.

The statement “You’re saving ₹1,796 on transfer charges and forex rates” also creates the impression that the conversion is highly competitive, while the displayed exchange rate appears materially higher than the prevailing market rate.

I request INDmoney to clearly disclose how this exchange rate is determined and what portion of the difference represents the bank’s forex spread. Customers should be able to see a transparent calculation before approving the transaction.

Please improve the transparency of USD/INR conversion rates and ensure customers receive a fair and properly evaluated exchange rate.

text:

My iPhone 11 is still running a supported/current iOS version and works perfectly well with other UPI and financial apps. If this is a security decision, the requirement should ideally be based on the supported iOS/security version rather than an arbitrary iPhone model.

Other platforms such as Groww continue to support UPI on iPhone 11. Because of this restriction, I am now considering moving my IPO and investment activities to another platform.

Unfortunately, with this decision, INDmoney may have lost two customers — mine and my wife’s.

I hope INDmoney reconsiders this policy and provides support for iPhone 11 rather than forcing customers to change their devices or platforms.

title: Feature Request: Transform INDmoney into a Complete Wealth Operating System
text:
I’ve been using INDmoney extensively and I believe it is already one of the best wealth aggregation platforms in India. The ability to track bank accounts, investments, net worth, family accounts, Indian stocks, US stocks, mutual funds, EPF, NPS and other assets in one place is extremely valuable.

However, there is a major opportunity to evolve INDmoney from a wealth tracker into a complete Personal Wealth Operating System.

Key feature gaps I would love to see:

1. Custom Transaction Categorization

* Allow users to create their own Categories and Subcategories.
* Example: Income → Salary, Bonus, Dividend.
* Expense → Food, Travel, Medical, Shopping.
* Investment → Mutual Fund SIP, Stock Purchase, Gold Purchase.

2. Full Budgeting System

* Monthly Budget vs Actual.
* Category-wise spending analysis.
* Savings rate and investment rate tracking.
* Cash flow forecasting.

3. Money Flow Tracking

* Track complete money movement across accounts.
* Example:
    Savings Account → INDmoney Wallet → USD Conversion → US Stock Purchase → Sale → Wallet → Bank Account.
* Every rupee and dollar should have a traceable journey.

4. Account Management Hub

* Maintain all bank accounts, broker accounts, wallet accounts and important account information.
* Track balances automatically from transactions.

5. Advanced Portfolio Rebalancing

* User-defined target allocation.
* Show current allocation vs target allocation.
* Recommend exact buy/sell actions.
* Tax-efficient rebalancing using future contributions.

6. Portfolio Drift Monitoring

* Alert users when allocations drift beyond a chosen threshold.
* Example: Equity target 60%, current 70%.

7. Financial Health Score

* Score based on:
    * Savings rate
    * Emergency fund
    * Diversification
    * Debt levels
    * Goal progress
    * Asset allocation
* Provide actionable recommendations.

8. Goal Planning

* Retirement
* House Purchase
* Child Education
* Vacation
* Emergency Fund

Show target amount, current progress and projected completion date.

9. Financial Independence Dashboard

* FI/FIRE progress tracker.
* Passive income tracking.
* Years to financial independence.
* Required corpus calculations.

10. More Powerful Web Platform
    The web app has huge potential.
    Please consider:

* Custom dashboards
* Drag-and-drop widgets
* Advanced portfolio analytics
* Portfolio drill-down reports
* Exportable reports
* Multi-monitor friendly layouts
* Professional investor dashboards

11. Multi-Currency Reporting
    Many users invest globally.
    Allow users to choose a Master Reporting Currency (INR, USD, EUR, GBP, etc.) and see net worth, gains, allocations and reports automatically converted.
12. AI Wealth Coach using MCP
    Since INDmoney already supports Claude MCP, allow users to ask:

* Am I overallocated anywhere?
* How should I invest ₹50,000 this month?
* What is my biggest portfolio risk?
* What should I do to improve my financial health score?

INDmoney already aggregates data better than most competitors. Adding budgeting, cash flow, rebalancing, financial planning and financial independence tracking could make it the definitive personal finance platform for serious investors.

title: Poor Order Execution Causing Financial Loss
text:
Extremely poor and unacceptable trading experience with INDMoney.

I am a regular trader and I am deeply disappointed with the order execution quality of this platform. The app consistently executes BUY orders at prices higher than the displayed market price, while SELL orders are executed at prices lower than expected. This repeated slippage causes direct financial loss to users.

The most frustrating part is that even when the market moves in profit direction, the delayed execution and poor order matching reduce or completely destroy the gains. It feels like the platform is always one step behind the live market.

Major issues faced repeatedly:
1. Delayed order execution during active market hours  
2. Huge difference between shown price and executed price  
3. Poor intraday trading support  
4. Lagging charts and delayed response  
5. Unreliable for scalping and quick trades  
6. Direct losses caused due to platform inefficiency

For a financial trading application, execution speed and price accuracy are the most basic expectations. Unfortunately INDMoney fails badly in this area.

This app may be suitable only for passive investors, but for active traders it is highly risky and disappointing.

I request the INDMoney team to seriously investigate their execution engine and compensate users suffering losses due to such poor platform performance.

Until then, I strongly do not recommend this app to anyone who is serious about trading.

title: Essential Risk Management Feature Missing in INDmoney
text:
INDmoney is a solid platform overall, but there’s one critical feature missing that can seriously impact traders, especially those who care about proper risk management.

Once a trade is placed, users should be able to set both Stop Loss (SL) and Take Profit (TP) orders at the same time. Right now, the limitation forces traders to manage positions manually or place orders separately, which increases risk and leaves room for error in fast moving markets.

This is not just a nice feature. It is essential. For traders, even a small delay or missed execution can make a big difference in outcomes. Having both SL and TP in place from the start ensures discipline, protects capital, and removes emotional decision making during volatility.

Another important point is that many traders prefer working with absolute numbers rather than percentages. Not everyone manages trades in percentages. Clear, number based inputs for SL and TP would make the platform more practical and user friendly for real trading scenarios.

A small upgrade like this could significantly improve the trading experience on INDmoney. It is about giving traders the control they need to manage risk properly.

title: Limited Flexibility in terms of Bank accounts
text: The main idea to invest in US stocks is to move a portion of your assets in another jurisdiction to avoid rupee depreciation and diversify the risk of holding all the assets in one country (India). This app does not allow the option to transfer money in to a foreign bank account once you sell your shares. This means that once you sell you need to convert back to Indian rupees and then again transfer back to USD to move the money to a foreign account. On a large portfolio this is lot of money lost in commision and conversion and the whole idea of keeping the money abroad is gone. You can rather use other US brokerage apps to buy these US shares who provide all the flexibility of adding any bank account and while selling there is no loss in conversion and commissions. This makes IND Money super market expensive in the longer term unless they give you option to add foreign bank accounts.

title: One of the most pathetic experiences I have ever had with a financial platform.
text:
Groww looks impressive until you actually need help. The moment there is a serious issue involving your money, the so-called “customer support” becomes an endless cycle of useless automated replies, copy-pasted messages and absolutely zero accountability.

It is honestly frustrating to see a financial platform put so much effort into making the app look smooth while seemingly putting so little effort into actually helping customers when something goes wrong.

You don’t feel like a customer—you feel like a ticket number being passed around by a system that doesn’t care whether your problem gets resolved or not.

When money is involved, “please wait” and generic replies are NOT customer service.

The entire experience has been unbelievably frustrating, time-consuming and disappointing. If you expect quick resolution, proper communication and someone to actually take ownership of your issue, don’t expect much from Groww.

I seriously regret choosing this platform. A financial service should give customers confidence and peace of mind—not make them constantly worry about whether their issue will ever be resolved.

Groww needs a reality check. A good-looking app cannot compensate for terrible support and a frustrating customer experience.

I would not recommend Groww based on my experience. There are better alternatives where customers deserve to be treated like customers.

title: Critical Issue: Chart Drawings and Trendlines Disappearing on Refresh
text:
I really appreciate the overall performance of the Kite app and web platform. The integration of advanced charts has been a game-changer. However, I am facing a persistent and frustrating issue that severely impacts daily trading.
 Problem: The trendlines, horizontal levels, and other technical drawings made on the charts do not save reliably. They frequently vanish simply by refreshing the page or switching timeframes/tabs.
 Technical trading relies entirely on continuous price action mapping, support, and resistance zones. Having hours of analysis wiped out mid-session ruins workflow, wastes critical time during live market hours, and introduces avoidable execution risks.
Trading is a game of precision and speed. Losing saved chart layouts defeats the purpose of advanced charting tools. Please look into this synchronization or saving bug on Kite's chart engine as a priority.

Go with brokers that don't penalize inactive accounts.

title: Kite app on iPad – Excellent charts, but the chart screen wastes the iPad's space
text:
As an active investor using kite on my iPad, I like the TradingView-powered charts, the indicators, and the quick Buy/Sell execution. The large screen is perfect for technical analysis, but the chart workflow doesn't take advantage of it.

The problem: When I'm analysing a stock on the chart screen, I can't move to the next stock directly. I have to go back, open my watchlist, tap the next stock, and then open its chart again. When screening 10-20 stocks in a session, this wastes time and breaks my analysis flow. Meanwhile, the iPad's wide landscape screen has plenty of unused space.

My request: Please add a collapsible watchlist panel on the right side of the chart screen in iPad landscape mode. One tap on any stock in the panel should load its chart instantly, keeping my timeframe, indicators, and layout. A swipe or arrow to jump to the next or previous stock in the watchlist would also help.

Why it matters: TradingView already offer this on tablets, and it's a standard feature for serious traders. It would save time and make kite iPad app a true trading workstation.

text:
Please make the SL update flow similar to Angel One.

Angel One provides a single input box, and the limit value is automatically updated based on the trigger value. In Zerodha, we currently have to update both the Limit Price and Trigger Price separately.

For quick intraday trades, this adds extra time and can cause missed entries. Please consider implementing the same single-input approach as Angel One, where the limit price is automatically adjusted when the trigger price is updated.

title: Serious order execution
text:
Extremely disappointing experience with this broker. I have lost thousands of rupees due to what appears to be an issue with order execution.
Orders are getting executed even though the price shown on the chart and the market depth does not appear to have reached my placed order price. This is extremely concerning, especially when trading involves real money and even a small difference in execution can result in significant losses.
I have personally suffered thousands of rupees in losses because of these executions. When the chart and market depth show that the specified price was not reached, an order should not be executed at that price without a clear and verifiable explanation.
A trading platform must provide accurate, transparent, and reliable order execution. Traders cannot be expected to trust a broker when their orders appear to be executed at prices that are not reflected in the displayed market data.
I strongly recommend that the broker investigate these executions, provide complete order/exchange execution details, and explain why the orders were triggered despite the displayed price not reaching the specified level.

title: Request to Add Trailing Stop Loss and Trailing Target in Kite App
text:
Hi Zerodha Team,

It would be extremely helpful if Kite could support trailing stop loss and trailing target functionality directly within regular order placement. Currently, users have to manually modify orders, which becomes difficult during fast market movements.

Suggested features:
- Trailing Stop Loss based on points or percentage  
- Trailing Target (profit lock-in as price moves favorably)  
- Ability to set both SL and Target together with trailing option  
- Applicable for intraday as well as delivery orders  
- Optional toggle inside bracket / GTT / regular orders  

This feature would significantly improve risk management and reduce the need for constant monitoring, especially for active traders.

Many modern trading platforms already provide trailing exits, and having this in Kite would make order execution much more efficient.

Please consider adding this in a future update.

title: The app does not show a portfolio-level “Invested vs Current Value” time-based chart
text:
Paytm Money is a good investment app overall. SIP execution is smooth, data is accurate, and the interface is clean and easy to use.

However, there is one major missing feature that becomes frustrating for long-term investors.

👉 The app does not show a portfolio-level “Invested vs Current Value” time-based chart.
Only individual mutual fund charts are available, but there is no combined portfolio growth chart to visually track how the entire portfolio has grown over time.

While numbers like invested amount, returns, and XIRR are shown,
visualizing the portfolio journey is not possible, which is important for understanding performance and making better decisions.

Apps like Groww and Zerodha already provide this feature.
Paytm Money should add a portfolio growth chart to improve the long-term investing experience.

With this improvement, the app can become much stronger.

title: Missing Bond Details After Update
text:
I have been using Paytm Money for bond investments, and until recently, it was very convenient. However, after the latest update, I noticed a serious issue: the detailed information for bonds I already purchased is missing.

Earlier, I could easily view key details like coupon rate, yield to maturity (YTM), maturity date, and issuer information for all my holdings. Now, this information is no longer visible in the app. Without these details, it is extremely difficult to track and manage my existing bond portfolio, or make informed decisions about redemptions and reinvestments.

For any serious bond investor, this data is essential. I strongly request Paytm Money to restore full visibility of bond details for purchased holdings at the earliest. Otherwise, the app loses much of its usefulness for fixed-income investors.

title: Issue in payment gateway
text:
I believe the app was comfortable earlier. 3 issues i would like to highlight:-
1. The payment gateway has become ultra trash for a company like paytm. I pay via netbanking, amt gets debited, when the bank screen redirects to paytmoney, it shows “something went wrong” and investment is rejected. Multiple times on multiple days it has happened. Okay, then i switch over to gpay, payment get done, no automatic redirect, i open the app, it shows payment successful - great. Then if i click ‘back’ or ‘discover more funds’, the app redirects me to gpay again and initiated payment prompt again on gpay to pay the same amt i just paid. I close every window, restart the app. Then it becomes ok. I mean, WHAT IS GOING ON? An Investment app so huge but cant design its payment gateways properly? Pathetic

2. The app seeks face id at every other step. Once we open the app with face id, i dont know why everytime i open portfolio it asks again and again. This depth of security is not understood.

3. I have invested more than 20L fm this app and the type of customer service paytm money offers is atrocious. It gives me chills and scares me. We are investing so much, and there is no proper method to contact ur service, the chats are useless, nobody responds, the calls get cut after 10 seconds, after waiting for 10 minutes. 

I truly cant be more polite than this. Please rectify app related issue and make us more easy as customer to reach to customer support. We have literally no interest in raising issues via ur 24x7 ai chatbot cause it’s a showoff and is useless.

title: Good Investment App but Needs Performance Improvements
text:
I have been using ET Money for the last few years for investing, and overall the experience has been good. The app offers useful investment features and a clean interface. However, there are still a few areas that need significant improvement.

A dark mode option would be highly appreciated, especially since most modern trading and investment apps already support it. It would improve the overall user experience during long usage sessions.

Additionally, the app performance needs optimization. Currently, the app takes quite a long time to load, and navigation feels slow at times. Faster loading and smoother performance would make the experience much better.

Looking forward to seeing these improvements in future updates.

title: App Usability Has Degraded Considering Switching Platforms
text:
I’ve been using this app since 2019, but over the past few years, the overall experience has significantly deteriorated. The app now seems flooded with "Genius" options and other paid features, making it difficult to access even basic information.
Simple mutual fund details, which were once easy to find, now require multiple clicks and navigation. Portfolio diversification insights, which were previously available to all users, are now locked behind the Genius membership.
I’ve tried the Genius membership before but didn’t find any standout value in it, so I chose not to renew.
At this point, I’m seriously considering moving all my investments to another platform. The app no longer opens to a clean, informative dashboard, it immediately pushes paid features instead.
It feels like self-managed mutual fund investors are no longer a priority for ET Money.

title: Customer Support Has Declined After the CRED Takeover
text:
I have been using Kuvera for some time and previously had a very positive experience with the platform, especially with its customer support.

However, after the CRED takeover, my recent experience has been quite disappointing. I had several concerns regarding my account and the application, but getting assistance from customer support has been extremely slow. There were instances where I had to wait for days without receiving a proper response, which was frustrating, particularly when dealing with matters related to investments and account information.

Kuvera has been a very good investment platform, and I genuinely hope the team takes customer support more seriously and restores the level of service and responsiveness it was previously known for.

I would be happy to revise my rating if the customer service experience improves.

Wishing the Kuvera team the best and hoping to see the platform return to its previous standards.

title: Serious Investors Need the Old Features Back
text:
The new Kuvera update feels like a downgrade in terms of usability and research features.

The older version was actually much better for serious mutual fund investors. A few important features seem to be missing now:

• Earlier, we could see 1D change for each individual mutual fund. Now it only shows overall portfolio 1D change, which reduces visibility into individual fund performance.

• Peer comparison details are gone. Previously, we could easily check where a mutual fund ranked within its category and compare it against category averages. That feature was extremely useful for analysis.

• Fund exploration and filtering also feels limited now. Earlier it was easier to browse and filter funds based on our own requirements.

The new UI may look cleaner, but a lot of practical investor-focused insights from the old version are missing. Would really appreciate if these features could be brought back.

Otherwise, users looking for detailed analysis and fund comparison may eventually prefer alternatives like INDmoney or similar platforms.

title: The New Update Removes What I Liked
text:
I have been on Kuvera for about 7-8 years now and I used to love Kuvera because it cleanly showed only the mutual fund investments I made through the app—simple, focused, and perfect for tracking my direct SIPs and transactions without clutter. The latest update changes this by forcing aggregation of all mutual fund investments from every platform (Zerodha, Groww, etc.), which I really don’t like.
This “all-in-one view” adds unwanted noise. I already check other apps for my external holdings—why complicate Kuvera by mixing them in? Now, my portfolio view is bloated with investments I didn’t make through Kuvera, making it harder to quickly see what matters: my direct investments on this platform.
My request is straightforward: bring back two separate views. One for “All Investments” (if you want aggregation), and one for “Kuvera-only” (my preferred default). Without this toggle, the app feels less useful to me.
Until they fix this, I’d recommend Kuvera only if you want full aggregation. If you, like me, prefer tracking solely your Kuvera investments, you might be disappointed.

title: Transactions Tracking and Payments Integration- Serious Issue
text:
Kuvera is definitely has lots of gaps. After using Kuvera as direct MF platform for past 1 year (almost), I would like to highlight some serious issues. List below. 
1) UPI integration is definitely not seamless. You are lucky, if there is a success. 30% it fails and you need to wait for reflection or initiate payment again. Kuvera doesn’t have proper tracking of UPI failures - instead you need to share all proofs for their support team to validate and complete the transactions.  Leads to serious frustration- when your funds are in dark and status unknown. 
2) When markets are highly volatile - avoid using Kuvera for MF investments. Even if you have success on the transaction, there is a possibility that your NAV is not of same day. Kuvera generally puts it back in BSEStar platform - which may be right, but for me I expected their platform to be resilient. Currently, stability is a serious issue. You lose if NaV is low for that day and Kuvera considers next days NaV. Also, to prove that your side of transactions are done perfectly - we need to share everything. In the digital world, I wouldn’t expect customer to keep on sharing proofs to Kuvera team to prove that transactions are correctly submitted. 
3) Support team has some gap in understanding queries. Many a times, multiple emails has to be triggered to explain the scenario and finally you get a response - which is completely out of context. 
4) I still struggle for transaction units which are lost through Kuvera - still don’t have a trace of what happened and kept proving that it’s missing. Analysis and response from support is definitely a concern. 
5) Kuvera is still not in a matured state and would expect them to standardise their operations, support, stability, resilience and finally transactions tracking seamlessly.
